cause: Tracking receiver required two multipart frames; the existing Kinefly ROS bridge sends a single JSON frame. Ports were loaded correctly, but valid payloads were rejected.

beforeFix.failurePhase: single-frame Kinefly JSON on four configured ports

wireRegression.coverage: Four configured ports, single JSON Kinefly bridge frames, multipart topic+JSON, independent topic/JSON messages, yaw-only fields, metadata, signed raw flight gains, malformed-packet recovery, separate telemetry, explicit HUD mode/endpoints, invalid monitoring config isolation, missing-rig endpoint retention, clean shutdown

historicalFlight.comparison: Exact Vector3 and Quaternion component equality on every simulated frame

headingTelemetry.coverage: Circular statistics, disabled/default/invalid/sequence config, generic and Choice adapters, real Swarm lifecycle, per-rig onset/no reset, repeat trial, PUB/SUB tracking and telemetry, raw units, player errors and HUD

editorMessages:
ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Index was out of range. Must be non-negative and less than the size of the collection.
Parameter name: index

standalonePlayerReplay.publisher: Unmodified process_ros_message function extracted from local Kinefly_Docker/_internal/ros_zmq_bridge.py; synthetic ROS wing angles

notes: Standalone macOS Development/Mono build included ControlScene and Swarm; headless player ran the production listener/controller/telemetry scripts and a disposable timed shutdown helper.
Synthetic ROS messages were passed to the existing unmodified process_ros_message function and sent using pyzmq over four localhost ports (29871-29874), with telemetry received separately on 29880.
Build succeeded with 65 warnings, including obsolete Unity APIs and the existing unsupported System.Windows.Forms assembly reference; no build errors.
Unity Editor search-index exception and existing No backup data file found startup message are recorded separately from regression failures.
A five-second read-only subscription received no packets from the configured physical Kinefly host. This does not verify the remote rig, network or LED timing.
Production hardware config and selected Selwyn experiment/terrain were not changed. No publisher update is required.
